sources.cloud.title: Connect cloud storage
sources.cloud.description: Super Ontology reads this bucket. It never changes or deletes anything in it.
sources.cloud.name: Name
sources.cloud.accountId.help: The 32-character account ID from your R2 dashboard.
sources.cloud.endpoint.bad: Use an https:// address (http:// only for this computer).
sources.cloud.prefix.help: Only files under this path are read. Leave empty for the whole bucket.
sources.cloud.readonly: Keys are stored in a private file on this computer and are not shown again.
sources.db.title: Connect a database
sources.db.description: Super Ontology reads the tables you list. It never writes to the database.
sources.db.host.help: The server address, for example db.internal.
sources.db.password.help: Kept in a private file on this computer and not shown again.
sources.db.ca.help: Paste the certificate authority that signed the server's certificate. The connection is always encrypted and verified.
sources.db.tables.help: One per line, as schema.table. Use schema.* for every table of a schema.
sources.db.remove.title: Remove {name}?
sources.db.remove.body: The saved password and certificate are deleted from this computer. The database itself is not touched.
sources.databases.title: Databases
sources.cloud.name.help: How this source is called in the app.
sources.cloud.bucket.help: The bucket name only, without s3:// or a path.
sources.cloud.accessKey.help: Created in your provider's console. Read-only access is enough.
sources.cloud.secretKey.help: Shown by the provider once, when the key was created.
sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Everything Super Ontology reads. Files you add stay on this computer.
sources.empty.title: Add your first source
sources.empty.body: Drop files here or pick a folder. Super Ontology reads them, finds the people, projects and decisions in them, and keeps every fact tied to where it came from.
sources.failed: {count, plural, one {# file couldn't be read} other {# files couldn't be read}}
sources.failed.body: The rest is unaffected. Open a file to see why and try again.
sources.files.empty.title: No files yet
sources.files.empty.body: Add files and they appear here while they are read.
sources.files.empty.readonly: This bucket has no files under the chosen folder, or they have not been read yet. Try Sync now.
sources.files.none.title: Nothing matches
sources.files.none.body: Change the search or the status filter.
sources.col.name: Name
sources.remove.title: Remove {name}?
sources.remove.body.folder: Super Ontology stops reading this folder and forgets what it learned from it. Your files are not touched.
sources.remove.body.cloud: Super Ontology stops reading this bucket and forgets what it learned from it. Nothing in the bucket is changed.
sources.panel.title: File details
ontology.title: Ontology
ontology.description: The people, projects and decisions Super Ontology found, and the evidence behind each fact.
ontology.none.title: No match
ontology.none.body: Try another name or clear the type filter.
ontology.empty.title: No entities yet
ontology.empty.body: Add sources first. Entities appear here as soon as the first files are understood.
ontology.nofacts.title: No facts yet
ontology.nofacts.body: Facts with evidence will appear here once they are published.
review.empty.title: Nothing to review
review.empty.body: When Super Ontology isn't sure about something, it waits for you here instead of guessing.
review.intro: Super Ontology was not sure about these. Nothing enters the ontology until you decide.
conflicts.empty.title: No rules yet
conflicts.empty.body: Rules the ontology checks itself against appear here.
agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Give an AI agent read-only access to what Super Ontology knows. Every answer it gets comes with its source.
connect.engine.title: The engine isn't running
connect.engine.body: Tokens are issued by the local engine. Start it from Settings, then come back.
connect.step1.title: 1. Create an access token
connect.step1.body: A token lets one agent read the ontology. It cannot change anything and you can revoke it at any time.
connect.name: Agent name
connect.name.help: Shown in the token list, so name it after the agent.
connect.drives.help: Limit it to one source if you prefer.
connect.ttl.help: After this the token stops working.
connect.step2.title: 2. Give it to your agent
connect.step2.body: Pick the agent you use and copy its configuration.
connect.once.title: Copy the token now
connect.once.body: It is shown only once and is not stored in the configuration. Keep it where your agent can read it.
connect.where.generic: Add this to the MCP servers of your client.
connect.where.claude: Run this once in a terminal to add the server to Claude.
connect.where.cursor: Save this as .cursor/mcp.json in your project, or in your home folder for every project.
connect.cli.title: The same from a terminal
connect.tokens.title: Tokens
connect.tokens.empty.title: No tokens yet
connect.tokens.empty.body: Tokens you create show up here so you can see who has access and revoke it.
connect.revoke.title: Revoke {name}?
connect.revoke.body: The agent stops being able to read immediately. This can't be undone; create a new token if you need access again.
packs.intro: A context pack is a short brief and its sources, prepared for one task and kept in a folder an agent can read.
packs.empty.title: No context packs yet
packs.empty.body: Create one for a task and an agent can pick it up from a folder.
packs.brief.title: Brief
packs.create.title: New context pack
packs.create.description: Write the brief for one task into a folder an agent can read.
packs.create.task: What is the agent working on?
packs.create.task.placeholder: For example, prepare the Atlas launch update
packs.create.task.help: The brief is tailored to this. Leave empty for a general overview.
packs.create.folder.help: The pack is written into a .context folder here.
access.intro: Who was given what, and when. This record is append-only.
access.intact.body: {count, plural, one {# entry was} other {# entries were}} checked and nothing has been changed.
access.empty.title: Nothing recorded yet
access.empty.body: When a context pack is created for an agent, it is recorded here.
connect.name.taken: This name is already in use.
settings.title: Settings
settings.language.title: Language
settings.language.body: Applies at once. Texts written by Super Ontology about your files stay in the language of the files.
settings.welcome.title: Welcome tour
settings.welcome.body: Go through the first-run steps again.
engine.oo.title: The oo command line isn't installed
engine.oo.body: Install it, or choose the oo program you already have.
engine.docker.body: Super Ontology can also run without Docker. Switch the runtime below to the built-in one, or start Docker and check again.
engine.runtime.help: Automatic uses Docker when it is running and the built-in runtime otherwise.
engine.keep: Keep the engine running when the app quits
engine.keep.help: Agents can keep reading while the app is closed.
model.optional.title: A model is optional
model.optional.body: Super Ontology reads every file with rules alone. Connect a model only if you want it to understand free-form text better; it then sees short excerpts of sources that allow it.
model.title: Model connection
model.none: No model connected. Rules are used for everything.
model.engine: Start the engine to see the model connection.
model.key.keep: Leave empty to keep the saved key.
model.key.note: The key is stored in a private file on this computer and is not shown again.
model.baseUrl.help: The address the provider gives for its API, often ending in /v1.
model.model.help: The model name exactly as the provider lists it.
model.dialog.title: Model connection
model.dialog.description: Any provider that speaks the OpenAI API, or Anthropic.
model.stale: It was changed somewhere else. Reopen this dialog and try again.
model.url.bad: Use an http:// or https:// address.
privacy.title: Where your data goes
privacy.body: This is computed from your current setup.
about.body: Turns your files and data into a typed, sourced, always-current knowledge layer that any agent can read with one token.
about.license.title: License
about.notices.body: Included with the app in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.
first.title: Welcome
first.welcome.title: Turn your files into knowledge an agent can use
first.welcome.body: Drop in documents. Super Ontology finds the people, projects and decisions in them, keeps every fact tied to its source, and lets any agent read it with a single token. Everything stays on this computer.
first.engine.help: You can fix this from Settings, then come back.
first.add.title: Add your first files
first.add.body: Start with a few documents: notes, meeting minutes, a spreadsheet.
first.add.local: They are copied into a folder this app manages.
first.add.waiting: One moment, the engine is still starting.
first.reading.title: Reading your files
first.reading.body: Each file is read, and the people, projects and decisions in it are found.
first.reading.waiting: Waiting for the files to arrive…
first.reading.leave: You can leave. It keeps going.
first.see.title: Here is what it found
first.see.body: Every fact points back to the sentence it came from.
first.agent.title: Give an agent access
first.agent.body: Create a read-only token, then copy the configuration into the agent you use.
home.next.explore.title: Explore what was found
home.next.explore.body: Open an entity to see its facts, each linked to the sentence it came from.
